title: Priming runbook weekly sketch — edge & region priming
content:
Purpose: capture the informal notes from this week’s priming / prewarm experiments and sketch a short runbook patch for APAC edge. This is a working document — capture experiments, hypotheses, quick wins, and immediate action items.

Context / problem statement:
- Over last two weeks we observed 12–18% tail latency spikes in APAC edge pools during morning ramp (02:00–04:30 UTC). Not consistent with overall regional request surge — appears correlated with cold-starts on t4g/slot-topology churn and a new binpack policy rollout.
- Objective this week: reduce observed tail anomalies by 50% during ramp windows via priming and slot hedging without adding >6% steady-state cost.

Quick metrics snapshot (week-on-week):
- APAC edge avg utilization: 71% (up 4pp)
- Primed slot hit rate (prefix cache warm): 39% -> goal 65%
- Cold-start count (observed eligible jobs): 146/day -> target <60/day
- Cost delta from aggressive prewarm prototype: +4.8% (est)

Experiments run (notes & outcomes):
1) Progressive prewarm throttling (canary):
   - What: staggered prewarm across AZs (30s ramp per AZ) instead of all-at-once prewarm.
   - Why: reduce simultaneous long-tail priming IO and avoid local network spike causing slow kernel loads.
   - Result: tail spikes reduced by ~22% in canary AZ; median unaffected.
   - Notes: needs tuning on request-signal threshold; small increase in priming latency for first AZ.

2) Scoped prefix caching for common prompts:
   - What: persist top-30 prompt prefixes in KV cache per node for 12h windows for high-traffic routes.
   - Why: quick wins for PLG flows where same prefixes are heavy.
   - Result: primed hit rate for those routes jumped to ~78% and latency dropped 15–20% per request.
   - Caveat: memory pressure on smaller nodes; required eviction tuning.

3) Slot hedging by capacity banding:
   - What: maintain 6% spare capacity in APAC small-slot pools during predicted ramps.
   - Why: give a buffer for burst without triggering preemptible reclaims.
   - Result: reduced evictions but increased idle cost ~2.1%. Impact on overall cost within acceptable guardrails.

Failure / anomaly observations:
- Several nodes (older kernel versions) failed to honor KV cache persistence after warm restart — reverted kernel to earlier build fixed it. Action: validate kernel compatibility in release gating for prefix caching feature.
- Prewarm job saturating disk IO on AZ-a when multiple model variants prewarm at once — move to staggered schedule and add IO backoff to prewarm agent.

Decisions made (quick):
- Roll priming patch (prefix caching + staggered prewarm) to APAC canary fleet on Mon 2026-04-06 02:00 UTC.
- Keep slot-band hedging at 6% for next 4 weeks while we gather more rigged traffic samples.
- Do not enable aggressive prewarm that warms full model weights on every node (too costly). Keep targeted prefix caching only.

Runbook sketch (short actionable steps):
1) Detection:
   - Signal: GA: sustained ramp > 20% util change in 30m + cold-starts > 75/day for region.
   - Pager: infra-ops (rotation) if tail latency P99 increases by >40% relative to baseline for 15m.
2) Immediate mitigation (0–30m):
   - Shift incoming traffic to neighboring region if multi-region route exists and SLO allows.
   - Enable staggered prewarm (canary). Endpoint: prewarm-agent toggle set to 'staggered'.
3) Short-term (30m–6h):
   - Apply prefix-caching rule for top routes (use dashboard to pick top-30 by QPS).
   - Increase slot-band hedging to +6% for that pool via capacity-controller.
4) Medium-term (same-day):
   - Run disk IO backoff test for prewarm agent and patch if necessary.
   - Coordinate with release engineering to pin kernel build for nodes supporting KV persistence.
5) Postmortem (72h):
   - Capture metrics, cost delta, and customer-impact snippets; escalate to platform lead if goals not met.

Action items (owner — due):
- Diego Alvarez — add prewarm-agent IO backoff and flagging (due 2026-04-07).
- Iris Chen — create dashboard widget for "primed hit rate" and route selector (due 2026-04-06).
- Ethan Morales — run kernel-compat smoke tests for KV persistence across node types (due 2026-04-09).
- Maya Patel — update priming runbook with canary steps and rollback criteria, notify SRE rotation (due 2026-04-05).

Open questions / things to watch:
- How much steady-state cost elasticity does PM/sales accept for smaller enterprise customers if we maintain 6% hedging long-term? (Need product/finance input)
- Are there model variants we can deprioritize for prefix caching (memory vs. latency tradeoff)?
- Can we instrument per-route cold-start correlation to better target priming?

Notes to self / informal observations:
- Staggered prewarm seems the highest ROI with low effort.
- The prefix-caching approach felt low-risk and gave large wins for PLG flows — prioritize routes with >200 QPS prewarm candidate.
- Watch for memory fragmentation on A100 small instances if we push too many prefixes.

Appendix (short):
- Quick CLI commands used this week:
   - prewarm-agent toggle set --pool apac-edge --mode staggered --grace 30s
   - capacity-controller set --pool apac-edge-small --hedge 6% --duration 28d

- Raw links:
   - Canary logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/apac/canary-priming/2026-04-02
   - PR for prewarm agent IO backoff: https://github.com/redwood-inference/fleet-tools/pull/291
